cues.zh: 想象一下，你生活在1980年代，
cues.en: magine you were alive back in the 1980's,

cues.zh: 有人告诉你，计算机很快会接管一切：
cues.en: and were told that computers would soon take over everything:

cues.zh: 从购物、约会到股票市场，
cues.en: from shopping, to dating, and the stock market,

cues.zh: 数十亿人会通过一种网络连接起来，
cues.en: that billions of people would be connected via a kind of web,

cues.zh: 你会拥有一台手持设备，性能比超级计算机强几个数量级。
cues.en: that you would own a handheld device, orders of magnitudes more powerful than supercomputers.

cues.zh: 这听起来很荒谬，但后来，这一切都发生了。
cues.en: It would seem absurd, but then, all of it happened.

cues.zh: 科幻变成了我们的现实，而我们甚至习以为常。
cues.en: Science fiction became our reality, and we don't even think about it.

cues.zh: 今天，基因工程让我们处在类似的节点上。
cues.en: We're at a similar point today with genetic engineering.

cues.zh: 那么，我们来聊聊它。
cues.en: So, let's talk about it.

cues.zh: 它从何而来，我们现在在做什么，
cues.en: Where it came from, what we're doing right now,

cues.zh: 以及一项最近的突破，它将永远改变我们的生活方式和对正常的认知。
cues.en: and about a recent breakthrough, that will change how we live and what we perceive as normal, forever.

cues.zh: 人类已经对生命进行了数千年的工程改造。
cues.en: Humans have been engineering life for thousands of years.

cues.zh: 通过选择性育种，我们强化了动植物中有用的性状。
cues.en: Through selective breeding, we strengthened useful traits in plants and animals.

cues.zh: 我们对此非常擅长，却从未完全理解其原理。
cues.en: We became very good at this, but never fully understood how it worked.

cues.zh: 直到我们发现了生命的密码——脱氧核糖核酸，也就是DNA。
cues.en: Until we discovered the code of life, Deoxyribonucleic Acid—DNA.

cues.zh: 一种复杂分子，指导着一切生物的生长、发育、功能和繁殖。
cues.en: A complex molecule that guides the growth, development, function, and reproduction of everything alive.

cues.zh: 信息被编码在分子的结构中。
cues.en: Information is encoded in the structure of the molecule.

cues.zh: 四种核苷酸成对组合，构成携带指令的代码。
cues.en: Four nucleotides are paired and make up a code that carries instructions.

cues.zh: 改变指令，就会改变携带它的生物。
cues.en: Change the instructions and you change the being carrying it.

cues.zh: DNA一经发现，人们就试图改造它。
cues.en: As soon as DNA was discovered, people tried to tinker with it.

cues.zh: 20世纪60年代，科学家用辐射轰击植物，使遗传密码发生随机突变。
cues.en: In the 1960's, scientist bombarded plants with radiation to cause random mutations in the genetic code.

cues.zh: 其想法是纯凭运气获得有用的植物变异。
cues.en: The idea was to get a useful plant variation by pure chance.

cues.zh: 有时候它甚至真管用。
cues.en: Sometimes it actually worked too.

cues.zh: 在 70 年代，科学家将 DNA 片段植入细菌、植物和动物体内，
cues.en: In the 70's, scientists inserted DNA snippets into bacteria, plants, and animals

cues.zh: 进行研究和改造，用于科研、医疗、农业，甚至纯属娱乐。
cues.en: to study and modify them for research, medicine, agriculture, and for fun.

cues.zh: 最早的基因改造动物诞生于 1974 年，这让小鼠成为了标准科研工具，拯救了数百万人的生命。
cues.en: The earliest genetically modified animal was born in 1974, making mice a standard tool for research, saving millions of lives.

cues.zh: 到了 80 年代，技术开始走向商业化。第一个专利被授予了一种专门用来吸收石油的改造微生物。
cues.en: In the 80's, we got commercial. The first patent was given for a microbe engineered to absorb oil.

cues.zh: 如今，我们借助工程改造生物生产各种化学物质，
cues.en: Today we produce many chemicals by means of engineered life,

cues.zh: 比如救命的凝血因子、生长激素和胰岛素。
cues.en: like life-saving clotting factors, growth hormones, and insulin.

cues.zh: 在这之前，所有这些都只能从动物器官中提取。
cues.en: All things we had to harvest from the organs of animals before that.

cues.zh: 1994 年，第一批在实验室改造的食品上市销售：Flavr Savr 番茄，
cues.en: The first food modified in the lab went on sale in 1994: the Flavr Savr tomato,

cues.zh: 这种番茄通过植入额外的基因来抑制腐烂酶的积累，从而获得了更长的保质期。
cues.en: a tomato given a much longer shelf life where an extra gene that suppresses the build-up of a rotting enzyme.

cues.zh: 但转基因食品及其争议，值得单独做一期视频。
cues.en: But GM food and the controversy surrounding them deserve a video of their own.

cues.zh: 在 20 世纪 90 年代，人类工程学也曾有过短暂的尝试。
cues.en: In the 1990's, there was also a brief foray into human engineering.

cues.zh: 为了治疗母体不孕，诞生了携带来自 3 个人遗传信息的婴儿。
cues.en: To treat maternal infertility, babies were made that carried genetic information from 3 humans.

cues.zh: 这使他们成为有史以来第一批拥有 3 位遗传学父母的人类。
cues.en: Making them the first humans ever to have 3 genetic parents.

cues.zh: 如今，已经有了肌肉极度发达的猪、速生三文鱼、无毛鸡，还有透明蛙。
cues.en: Today there are super muscled pigs, fast-growing salmon, featherless chicken, and see-through frogs.

cues.zh: 好玩的是，我们还让生物能在黑暗中发光。
cues.en: On the fun side, we made things glow in the dark.

cues.zh: 荧光斑马鱼只要 10 美元就能买到。
cues.en: Fluorescent zebrafish are available for as little as ten dollars.

cues.zh: 这一切已经非常令人震撼了，但在不久之前，
cues.en: All of this is already very impressive, but until recently

cues.zh: 基因编辑还极其昂贵、复杂，而且非常耗时。
cues.en: gene editing was extremely expensive, complicated, and took a long time to do.

cues.zh: 而随着一项革命性新技术的登场，这一切都改变了——那就是 CRISPR。
cues.en: This has now changed with a revolutionary new technology now entering the stage—CRISPR.

cues.zh: 一夜之间，工程成本下降了99%。
cues.en: Overnight, the costs of engineering have shrunk by 99 %.

cues.zh: 实验不再需要一年，只需几周，基本上每个有实验室的人都能做。
cues.en: Instead of a year, it takes a few weeks to conduct experiments, and basically everybody with a lab can do it.

cues.zh: 很难说清CRISPR是一场多么重大的技术革命。
cues.en: It's hard to get across how big a technical revolution CRISPR is.

cues.zh: 它真的有可能永远改变人类。
cues.en: It literally has the potential to change humanity forever.

cues.zh: 这场突如其来的革命为何发生，又是如何运作的？
cues.en: Why did this sudden revolution happen and how does it work?

cues.zh: 自生命诞生之初，细菌和病毒就一直在斗争。
cues.en: Bacteria and viruses have been fighting since the dawn of life.

cues.zh: 所谓的噬菌体（phage）会捕食细菌。
cues.en: So-called bacteriophages or phages hunt bacteria.

cues.zh: 在海洋中，噬菌体每天杀死其中40%的细菌。
cues.en: In the ocean, phages kill 40 % of them every single day.

cues.zh: 噬菌体把自己的遗传密码插入细菌，接管它们，把它们当作工厂。
cues.en: Phages do this by inserting their own genetic code into the bacteria and taking them over to use them as factories.

cues.zh: 细菌试图抵抗，但大多数时候都失败了，因为它们的防护工具太弱，
cues.en: The bacteria tried to resist but failed most the time because their protection tools are too weak,

cues.zh: 但有时细菌能在攻击中存活下来。
cues.en: But sometimes bacteria survive an attack.

cues.zh: 只有这样，它们才能激活自己最有效的抗病毒系统：
cues.en: Only if they do so can they activate their most effective antivirus system:

cues.zh: 它们会把病毒DNA的一部分存入自身的遗传密码中，保存在一个叫CRISPR的DNA档案库里。
cues.en: they save a part of the virus DNA in their own genetic code in a DNA archive called CRISPR.

cues.zh: 它被安全地存放在这里，直到需要时才动用。
cues.en: Here it's stored safely until it's needed.

cues.zh: 当病毒再次来袭时，细菌会迅速从DNA档案库复制出一份RNA，并启动一件秘密武器——一种叫CAS9的蛋白质。
cues.en: When the virus attacks again, the bacterium quickly makes an RNA copy from the DNA archive and arms a secret weapon—a protein called CAS9.

cues.zh: 这种蛋白质会扫描细菌内部，寻找病毒入侵者的踪迹
cues.en: The protein now scans the bacterium's insides for signs of the virus invader

cues.zh: 把它找到的每一段DNA与档案库中的样本逐一比对。
cues.en: by comparing every bit of DNA it finds to the sample from the archive.

cues.zh: 一旦找到100%完全匹配的目标，
cues.en: When it finds a 100-percent perfect match,

cues.zh: 它就会被激活，切掉病毒DNA，使其失效，从而保护细菌免受攻击。
cues.en: it's activated and cuts out the virus DNA, making it useless, protecting the bacterium against the attack.

cues.zh: 特别之处在于，CAS9非常精确，几乎就像一位DNA外科医生。
cues.en: What's special is that CAS9 is very precise, almost like a DNA surgeon.

cues.zh: 科学家发现CRISPR系统可编程时，这场革命就开始了。
cues.en: The revolution began when scientists figured out that the CRISPR system is programmable.

cues.zh: 你只需给它一份想要修改的DNA副本，再把系统放进活细胞里。
cues.en: You can just give it a copy of DNA you want to modify and put the system into a living cell.

cues.zh: 如果说旧的基因操作技术像一张地图，CRISPR就像GPS系统。
cues.en: If the old techniques of genetic manipulation were like a map, CRISPR is like a GPS system.

cues.zh: 除了精准、便宜、简单，CRISPR还能编辑活细胞，
cues.en: Aside from being precise, cheap, and easy, CRISPR offers the ability to edit live cells,

cues.zh: 开启和关闭基因，靶向并研究特定的DNA序列。
cues.en: to switch genes on and off, and target and study particular DNA sequences.

cues.zh: 它还适用于所有类型的细胞：微生物、植物、动物或人类。
cues.en: It also works for every type of cell: microorganisms, plants, animals, or humans.

cues.zh: 尽管CRISPR对科学是一场革命，它仍然只是第一代工具。
cues.en: But despite the revolution CRISPR is for science, it's still just a first generation tool.

cues.zh: 更精准的工具已经在被创造和使用，就在我们说话这会儿。
cues.en: More precise tools are already being created and used as we speak.

cues.zh: 2015年，科学家用CRISPR从实验室患者的活细胞中切除了HIV病毒，
cues.en: In 2015, scientists use CRISPR to cut the HIV virus out of living cells

cues.zh: 证明了这是可行的。
cues.en: from patients in the lab, proving that it was possible.

cues.zh: 大约一年后，他们开展了一个更大规模的项目，用大鼠做实验
cues.en: Only about a year later, they carried out a larger scale project with rats

cues.zh: 这些大鼠几乎所有体细胞中都带有HIV病毒。
cues.en: that had the HIV virus in basically all of their body cells.

cues.zh: 仅仅通过向大鼠尾部注射CRISPR，
cues.en: By simply injecting CRISPR into the rats tails,

cues.zh: 他们就能清除全身细胞中超过50%的病毒。
cues.en: they were able to remove more than 50 % of the virus from cells all over the body.

cues.zh: 几十年内，CRISPR疗法或许就能治愈HIV和其他逆转录病毒，
cues.en: In a few decades, a CRISPR therapy might cure HIV and other retroviruses,

cues.zh: 像疱疹这样隐藏在人类DNA中的病毒，也能用这种方式根除。
cues.en: viruses that hide inside human DNA like Herpes could be eradicated this way.

cues.zh: CRISPR还能击败我们最凶恶的敌人之一——癌症。
cues.en: CRISPR could also defeat one of our worst enemies—cancer.

cues.zh: 癌症的发生，是因为细胞拒绝死亡、不断增殖，同时躲避免疫系统的监视。
cues.en: Cancer occurs when cells refuse to die and keep multiplying while concealing themselves from the immune system.

cues.zh: CRISPR让我们有能力编辑免疫细胞，把它们改造成更强的癌症猎手。
cues.en: CRISPR gives us the means to edit your immune cells and make them better cancer hunters.

cues.zh: 消灭癌症最终可能意味着
cues.en: Getting rid of cancer might eventually mean

cues.zh: 只需注射几次、每次几千个你自己的细胞
cues.en: getting just a couple of injections of a few thousand of your own cells

cues.zh: 这些细胞已在实验室中被改造，能彻底治愈你。
cues.en: that have been engineered in the lab to heal you for good.

cues.zh: 2016年初，美国批准了首个针对人类患者的CRISPR癌症治疗临床试验。
cues.en: The first clinical trial for a CRISPR cancer treatment on human patients was approved in early 2016 in the US.

cues.zh: 不到一个月后，中国科学家宣布，他们将于2016年8月
cues.en: Not even a month later, Chinese scientists announced that they would treat lung cancer patients

cues.zh: 用经CRISPR修饰的免疫细胞治疗肺癌患者。
cues.en: with immune cells modified with CRISPR in August 2016.

cues.zh: 事情进展得很快。
cues.en: Things are picking up pace quickly.

cues.zh: 此外还有遗传疾病。
cues.en: And then there are genetic diseases.

cues.zh: 这类疾病有数千种，从轻微恼人到致命，或带来数十年的痛苦。
cues.en: There are thousands of them and they range from mildly annoying to deadly or entail decades of suffering.

cues.zh: 有了CRISPR这样强大的工具，我们或许能终结这一切。
cues.en: With a powerful tool like CRISPR, we may be able to end this.

cues.zh: 超过3000种遗传疾病是由DNA中一个错误的字母引起的。
cues.en: Over 3,000 genetic diseases are caused by a single incorrect letter in your DNA.

cues.zh: 我们已经在构建一个改良版的CAS9，它被设计用来只改变一个字母，从而在细胞中修复疾病。
cues.en: We are already building a modified version of CAS9 that is made to change just a single letter, fixing the disease in the cell.

cues.zh: 再过一二十年，我们或许就能彻底治愈数千种疾病。
cues.en: In a decade or two, we could possibly cure thousands of diseases forever.

cues.zh: 但所有这些医疗应用都有一个共同点：
cues.en: But all of these medical applications have one thing in common:

cues.zh: 它们仅作用于个体，并随个体的死亡而终结，
cues.en: they are limited to the individual and die with them,

cues.zh: 除非将其用于生殖细胞或极早期的胚胎。
cues.en: except if you use them on reproductive cells or very early embryos.

cues.zh: 但 CRISPR 能够、而且很可能被用于更多领域：
cues.en: But CRISPR can and probably will be used for much more:

cues.zh: 比如创造经过基因改造的人类——“定制婴儿”——这也意味着
cues.en: the creation of modified humans—designer babies—and will mean gradual,

cues.zh: 人类基因库将发生渐进但不可逆的改变。
cues.en: but irreversible changes to the human gene pool.

cues.zh: 编辑人类胚胎基因组的技术手段其实已经存在。
cues.en: The means to edit the genome of a human embryo already exists.

cues.zh: 虽然这项技术仍处于起步阶段，但目前已经尝试过两次了。
cues.en: Though the technology is still in its early stages, but it has already been attempted twice.

cues.zh: 在 2015 和 2016 年，中国科学家在人类胚胎上进行了实验，并在第二次尝试中取得了部分成功。
cues.en: In 2015 and 2016, Chinese scientists experimented with human embryos and were partially successful on their second attempt.

cues.zh: 这表明我们在胚胎基因编辑方面仍面临巨大挑战，
cues.en: They showed the enormous challenges we still face in gene editing embryos,

cues.zh: 但也说明科学家们正在努力攻克它们。
cues.en: but also that scientists are working on solving them.

cues.zh: 这就像 70 年代的计算机，未来一定会有更好的计算机出现。
cues.en: This is like the computer in the 70's. There will be better computers.

cues.zh: 无论你个人对基因工程持何种看法，它都会影响到你。
cues.en: Regardless of your personal take on genetic engineering, it will affect you.

cues.zh: 被改造的人类可能会改变我们整个物种的基因组，因为他们被编辑的性状会遗传给后代，
cues.en: Modified humans could alter the genome of our entire species, because their engineered traits will be passed on to their children

cues.zh: 并可能代代相传，慢慢改变整个人类的基因库。
cues.en: and could spread over generations, slowly modifying the whole gene pool of humanity.

cues.zh: 这一切会来得很缓慢。第一批“设计婴儿”不会被过度设计。
cues.en: It will start slowly. The first designer babies will not be overly designed.

cues.zh: 更有可能的是，他们是为了消除家族遗传的致命基因疾病而被创造出来的。
cues.en: It's most likely that they will be created to eliminate a deadly genetic disease running in a family.

cues.zh: 随着技术的进步和日益完善，越来越多的人可能会认为，不用基因改造技术是不道德的，
cues.en: As the technology progresses and gets more refined, more and more people may argue that not using genetic modification is unethical,

cues.zh: 因为这等于让孩子遭受本可避免的痛苦和死亡，剥夺了他们治愈的权利。
cues.en: because it condemns children to preventable suffering and death and denies them the cure.

cues.zh: 但一旦第一个经过基因工程的孩子出生，就打开了一扇再也关不上的门。
cues.en: But as soon as the first engineered kid is born, a door is opened that can't be closed anymore.

cues.zh: 早期，那些虚荣性的特征大多不会被改动。
cues.en: Early on, vanity traits will mostly be left alone.

cues.zh: 但随着基因改造变得越来越被接受，我们对基因密码的认识不断加深，诱惑也会越来越大。
cues.en: But as genetic modification becomes more accepted and our knowledge of our genetic code enhances, the temptation will grow.

cues.zh: 如果你能让后代对阿尔茨海默病免疫，为什么不顺便给他们增强的新陈代谢呢？
cues.en: If you make your offspring immune to Alzheimer, why not also give them an enhanced metabolism?

cues.zh: 为什么不加上完美的视力呢？
cues.en: Why not throw in perfect eyesight?

cues.zh: 身高或肌肉结构怎么样？
cues.en: How about height or muscular structure?

cues.zh: 浓密的头发？
cues.en: Full hair?

cues.zh: 给孩子一份非凡智力的礼物怎么样？
cues.en: How about giving your child the gift of extraordinary intelligence?

cues.zh: 巨大的变化正是由数百万个体的个人决定累积而成的。
cues.en: Huge changes are made as a result of the personal decisions of millions of individuals that accumulate.

cues.zh: 这是一条滑坡。改造过的人类可能成为新的标准。
cues.en: This is a slippery slope. Modified humans could become the new standard.

cues.zh: 但随着基因工程变得越来越寻常、我们的知识不断进步，
cues.en: But as engineering becomes more normal and our knowledge improves,

cues.zh: 我们就能解决最大的单一死亡风险因素：衰老。
cues.en: we could solve the single biggest mortality risk factor: aging.

cues.zh: 今天死亡的 15 万人中，有三分之二死于衰老相关的原因。
cues.en: Two-thirds of the 150,000 people who died today will die of age-related causes.

cues.zh: 目前我们认为，衰老是细胞损伤累积导致的，
cues.en: Currently we think aging is caused by the accumulation of damage to our cells,

cues.zh: 比如 DNA 断裂，以及负责修复的系统随着时间推移逐渐失效。
cues.en: like DNA breaks and the systems responsible for fixing those wearing off over time.

cues.zh: 但也有一些基因会直接影响衰老。
cues.en: But there are also genes that directly affect aging.

cues.zh: 基因工程与其他疗法的结合，可以阻止或延缓衰老，甚至可能实现逆转。
cues.en: A combination of genetic engineering and other therapy could stop or slow down aging, maybe even reverse it.

cues.zh: 我们从大自然中得知，有些动物对衰老是免疫的。
cues.en: We know from nature that there are animals immune to aging.

cues.zh: 或许我们甚至能为自己借用一些基因。
cues.en: Maybe we could even borrow a few genes for ourselves.

cues.zh: 有些科学家甚至认为，生理衰老最终可能根本不再是个问题。
cues.en: Some scientists even think biological aging could be something that eventually just stops being a thing.

cues.zh: 我们到头来还是会死，但不再是 90 岁躺在医院里离开，
cues.en: We would still die at some point, but instead of doing so in hospitals at age 90,

cues.zh: 而是可能和我们所爱的人一起度过几千年。
cues.en: we might be able to spend a few thousand years with our loved ones.

cues.zh: 这方面的研究还处于起步阶段，
cues.en: Research into this is in its infancy,

cues.zh: 许多科学家有理由对终结衰老持怀疑态度。
cues.en: and many scientists are rightly skeptical about the end of aging.

cues.zh: 挑战巨大，也许根本无法实现，
cues.en: The challenges are enormous and maybe it is unachievable,

cues.zh: 但可以想象，今天活着的人或许会成为首批受益于有效抗衰老疗法的人。
cues.en: but it is conceivable the people alive today might be the first to profit from effective anti aging therapy.

cues.zh: 我们可能只需要有人说服一位聪明的亿万富翁，把它当作下一个要解决的问题。
cues.en: All we might need is for someone to convince a smart billionaire to make it their next problem to solve.

cues.zh: 在更大尺度上，通过改造人群，我们确实能解决很多问题。
cues.en: On a bigger scale, we certainly could solve many problems by having a modified population.

cues.zh: 经过工程化改造的人类可能更能适应高能量食物，
cues.en: Engineered humans might be better equipped to cope with high-energy food,

cues.zh: 从而消除肥胖等许多文明病。
cues.en: eliminating many diseases of civilization like obesity.

cues.zh: 拥有改造过的免疫系统，并配有一个潜在威胁库，
cues.en: In possession of a modified immune system, with a library of potential threats,

cues.zh: 我们或许能对如今困扰我们的大多数疾病免疫。
cues.en: we might become immune to most diseases that haunt us today.

cues.zh: 再往未来看，我们可以改造人类，让他们适应长途太空旅行
cues.en: Even further into the future, we could engineer humans to be equipped for extended space travel

cues.zh: 并能应对其他星球上的不同环境，
cues.en: and to cope with different conditions on another planets,

cues.zh: 这对我们在充满敌意的宇宙中生存下去极为有利。
cues.en: which would be extremely helpful in keeping us alive in our hostile universe.

cues.zh: 不过，还有几个重大挑战等着我们：有些是技术上的，有些是伦理上的。
cues.en: Still, a few major challenges await us: some technological, some ethical.

cues.zh: 观看的许多人会感到不安，担心我们会创造一个世界，在其中排斥不完美的人类，
cues.en: Many of you watching will feel uncomfortable and fear that we will create a world in which we will reject non-perfect humans

cues.zh: 并根据我们对健康的理解来预先筛选特征和品质。
cues.en: and pre-select features and qualities based on our idea of what's healthy.

cues.zh: 问题是，我们其实已经生活在这个世界里了。
cues.en: The thing is we are already living in this world.

cues.zh: 在世界许多地方，针对数十种遗传疾病或并发症的检测已成为孕妇的常规项目。
cues.en: Tests for dozens of genetic diseases or complications have become standard for pregnant women in much of the world.

cues.zh: 往往仅仅怀疑有基因缺陷，就可能导致终止妊娠。
cues.en: Often the mere suspicion of a genetic defect can lead to the end of a pregnancy.

cues.zh: 以唐氏综合征为例，这是最常见的遗传缺陷之一。
cues.en: Take Down syndrome for example, one of the most common genetic defects.

cues.zh: 在欧洲，大约92%检测出该缺陷的怀孕会被终止。
cues.en: In Europe, about 92 % of all pregnancies where it's detected are terminated.

cues.zh: 终止妊娠的决定极其个人化，
cues.en: The decision to terminate pregnancy is incredibly personal,

cues.zh: 但必须正视一个现实：我们正在依据医学状况对人类进行预筛选。
cues.en: but it's important to acknowledge the reality that we are pre-selecting humans based on medical conditions.

cues.zh: 假装这一切不会改变也没有意义，
cues.en: There is also no use in pretending this will change,

cues.zh: 所以随着技术进步、能做出越来越多选择，我们必须谨慎而尊重地行事。
cues.en: so we have to act carefully and respectfully as we advance the technology and can make more and more selections.

cues.zh: 但这一切不会很快发生。
cues.en: But none of this will happen soon.

cues.zh: 尽管CRISPR非常强大——它确实强大，但还并非万无一失。
cues.en: As powerful as CRISPR is—and it is, it's not infallible yet.

cues.zh: 错误编辑仍会发生，未知错误也可能出现在DNA的任何位置，且可能不被察觉。
cues.en: Wrong edits still happen as well as unknown errors that can occur anywhere in the DNA and might go unnoticed.

cues.zh: 基因编辑可能达到预期结果——让某种疾病失效，
cues.en: The gene edit might achieve the desired result—disabling a disease,

cues.zh: 但也可能意外触发不想要的改变。
cues.en: but also might accidentally trigger unwanted changes.

cues.zh: 我们对基因间复杂相互作用的了解还远远不够，无法避免不可预测的后果。
cues.en: We just don't know enough yet about the complex interplay of our genes to avoid unpredictable consequences.

cues.zh: 随着首批人体试验的开始，提高精准度和监测手段成了重中之重。
cues.en: Working on accuracy and monitoring methods is a major concern as the first human trials begin.

cues.zh: 既然我们畅想了光明的未来，那自然也有更黑暗的可能。
cues.en: And since we've discussed a possible positive future, there are darker visions too.

cues.zh: 设想一下，如果像朝鲜这样的国家全面拥抱基因工程，会发生什么。
cues.en: Imagine what a state like North Korea could do if they embraced genetic engineering.

cues.zh: 一个政权是否能通过强制臣民进行基因编辑，来永远巩固其统治？
cues.en: Could a state cement its rule forever by forcing gene editing on their subjects?

cues.zh: 又有什么能阻止极权政府去培育一支经过改造的超级士兵军团呢？
cues.en: What would stop a totalitarian regime from engineering an army of modified super soldiers?

cues.zh: 这在理论上是完全行得通的。
cues.en: It is doable in theory.

cues.zh: 哪怕这种场景真能实现，也是极其遥远的未来的事了。
cues.en: Scenarios like this one are far, far off into the future, if they ever become possible at all.

cues.zh: 但今天，这类基因工程的基础概念验证已经存在了。
cues.en: But the basic proof of concept for genetic engineering like this already exists today.

cues.zh: 这项技术确实就是有这么强大。
cues.en: The technology really is that powerful.

cues.zh: 虽然这可能会让人想禁止基因编辑及相关研究，但那肯定是个错误。
cues.en: While this might be a tempting reason to ban genetic editing and related research, that would certainly be a mistake.

cues.zh: 禁止人类基因工程，只会让这门科学流向
cues.en: Banning human genetic engineering would only lead to the science wandering off

cues.zh: 那些拥有我们不适应的管辖权和规则的地方。
cues.en: to a place with jurisdiction and rules that we are uncomfortable with.

cues.zh: 只有参与其中，我们才能确保后续研究受到谨慎、理性、监督和透明原则的引导。
cues.en: Only by participating can we make sure that further research is guided by caution, reason, oversight, and transparency.

cues.zh: 你现在觉得不舒服了吗？
cues.en: Do you feel uncomfortable now?

cues.zh: 我们大多数人身上都有点缺陷。
cues.en: Most of us have something wrong with them.

cues.zh: 在我们前方的未来里，我们还会被允许存在吗？
cues.en: In the future that lies ahead of us, would we have been allowed to exist?

cues.zh: 这项技术确实有点吓人，但我们能获益很多，
cues.en: The technology is certainly a bit scary, but we have a lot to gain,

cues.zh: 而基因工程也许只是宇宙中智能物种自然演化的一步。
cues.en: and genetic engineering might just be a step in the natural evolution of intelligent species in the universe.

cues.zh: 我们或许能终结疾病。
cues.en: We might end disease.

cues.zh: 我们可能把预期寿命延长几个世纪，还能遨游星际。
cues.en: We could extend our life expectancy by centuries and travel to the stars.

cues.zh: 在这个话题上，没必要把眼光放小。
cues.en: There's no need to think small when it comes to this topic.

cues.zh: 无论你对基因工程持什么看法，未来都在逼近，不可阻挡。
cues.en: Whatever your opinion on genetic engineering, the future is approaching no matter what.

cues.zh: 曾经的疯狂科幻，即将成为我们的新现实，
cues.en: What has been insane science fiction is about to become our new reality,

cues.zh: 一个充满机遇与挑战的现实。
cues.en: a reality full of opportunities and challenges.

cues.en: Videos like this would not be possible without viewer donations on patreon.com.

cues.en: If you want to support to explaining complicated stuff and maybe get your own bird in return, you can do so here.

cues.en: If you want to learn more about CRISPR, we put the sources and further reading in the description.

cues.en: More videos about the whole topic area will follow.

cues.en: If you want to be notified when it happens, you can follow us here.
